html:
The Erie were an Iroquoian people who lived south of Lake Erie, in what is now northern Ohio, northwestern Pennsylvania and western New York. The lake, and later the city of Erie, take their name from them. The French called them the Cat Nation, after the meaning usually given to their name.

They lived in palisaded farming villages of longhouses, growing maize, beans and squash, much like their Iroquoian relatives the Huron and the Neutral.

The Erie were destroyed in the Beaver Wars. In the 1650s the Haudenosaunee, armed with Dutch guns and seeking furs and captives, attacked them, after already breaking the Huron and the Neutral. By about 1657 the Erie had been defeated. Many were killed, and many others were taken in and adopted by the Seneca and other Haudenosaunee nations. The Erie never again appear as a separate people. The Susquehannock to the east held out longer.
